title: Problems with mi RTS
author: Juanhsc
selftext:
**Advice on building an RTS with AI: is it how I’m asking, or is it just not there yet?**

Hi everyone. I’m building an RTS with AI assistance and I could use some advice, because I can’t crack it.

I’ve already built adventure, shooter and fighting games without much trouble, but the RTS keeps defeating me. I’m using **Claude + Godot**, with **Blender** for models and **OpenAI** for images.

Where I specifically get stuck:

* **Terrain depth.** I can’t get it to understand how elevation works on an isometric map.
* **The overhead view.** It doesn’t quite grasp the camera angle this genre depends on.
* **Structure design.** I can’t get buildings that look like they belong to the same game.
* **Unit design and movement.** Neither facing the direction they’re walking, nor moving convincingly.

I don’t know what to blame, which is why I’m asking. It could be:

1. **Me**, because I don’t know how to explain what I want. If that’s the case and you know of a *skill* or a better way to structure these requests, I’d really appreciate the pointer.
2. **The tools**, if there are better ones for this.
3. **The state of the art**, if this simply isn’t something AI can do today without a lot of pain.

For reference, the games I love and want to emulate are **Command & Conquer**, **StarCraft** and **Battle for Middle-earth**.

Any advice is welcome.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
> **Me**, because I don’t know how to explain what I want.

It takes some humility to put that one first, congrats. Unfortunately, I think this is probably the biggest explanation.

Things like terrain depth—Claude doesn’t really need to understand terrain depth. If you can understand it, you can give Claude acceptance criteria for checking that it’s implemented terrain depth correctly. Things like, 

1. Every tile on the map has an elevation, which is an integer from 0 to 5,
2. When a unit attacks a unit, it gets bonuses if the attacker is at a higher elevation, or penalties if it's at a lower elevation,

Then I would make tools that can edit elevation in maps, I’d make it so elevation gets rendered correctly, etc. Skills don’t really help. It is all you. You have to be able to express a clear goal for the AI. You also have to break the goal into smaller steps that it can successfully complete.

The AI can help you write these criteria and help you break down the tasks, in an interactive session.

Keep in mind that the RTS is a very technically challenging genre of game to make, even with AI.

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body: From experience building my turn based strategy game with real time action replays, the camera angle and lighting is more important than the meshes, textures or anything else in getting the vision on the screen. Pitch and yaw! Yaw is incredibly important, 0 yaw is dead on the front face of every asset so buildings look flat. A small like 15 degrees yaw can completely transform the look of your game.

comments.author: Tom_Baron
comments.body:
Structure design with AI is really tricky too. Im not there either. I wrote an underlying asset vision of how i wanted my city to look, i got codex to draft a corpus of images then used these with an mcp to blender to create my initial meshes, sent these to meshy with mcp for texture then opus with mcp to blender and an alignment doc stating relative sizes of buildings (big context needed) for touching up. I still am not totally happy but the city view was so far advanced of everything else in my game i moved on to other areas. Ill return likely when a first pass of granular mechanic tuning is complete. 

If you want a good game, build a headless lab that lets you run multiple instances of your game engine concurrently. Build your variables into it, make NPCs and test versions of npcs that run certain strategies, think about how your game could be beaten or what interesting mechanics players could take advantage of and build these strategies into npcs, then expect to spend 1000s of hours in there experimenting and tuning. 

If you dont enjoy the tuning and analysis then building strategy games might not be for you 😅
